cases.sentence: Кружится у меня почему-то в ___ Антон Чехов.
cases.translation: For some reason Anton Chekhov is spinning round in my head.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (a location, not a direction) takes the prepositional case: в голове.

cases.sentence: Когда ему водку случалось пить, он ноги свои опускал в ___.
cases.translation: When he happened to be drinking vodka, he would lower his feet into champagne.
cases.explain: Here «в» means movement into something, which requires the accusative; шампанское is a neuter inanimate noun, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Он повалился на канделябр и так пошел по ___, гася огни.
cases.translation: He fell onto the candelabrum and went off down the carriage like that, putting out the lights.
cases.explain: «По» in the sense of moving along or around a place governs the dative: по вагону.

cases.sentence: Петр, все так же, не моргая и со ___, глядел на меня.
cases.translation: Pyotr went on staring at me just the same, without blinking and with malice.
cases.explain: «С» meaning 'with' in the sense of accompanying manner takes the instrumental; злобою is the older bookish variant of злобой.

cases.sentence: А когда очнулся – в вагоне не было ни ___.
cases.translation: And when I came to, there was not a soul in the carriage.
cases.explain: Negated existence with «не было» puts the missing thing in the genitive, and the intensifier «ни» reinforces it: ни души.

cases.translation: And it was a strange thought.
cases.explain: With «быть» in the past tense the predicate noun can stand in the nominative, agreeing with the subject это.

cases.sentence: Он дома у себя ходил в тапочках и ___.
cases.translation: At home he used to walk about in slippers and a dressing gown.
cases.explain: «В» describing the clothes someone is wearing answers «в чём?» and takes the prepositional: в шлафроке.

reading.question: What does Pyotr say when Venichka asks where his princess is?
options: That she got off long ago
That she is asleep in the next carriage
That she went to look for a drink
reading.correct: That she got off long ago
reading.explain: Pyotr answers flatly that she left the train a long time ago.

reading.ru: Она из Петушков ехала в Храпуново.
reading.question: Where was the princess travelling, according to Pyotr?
reading.explain: Pyotr says she was going from Petushki to Khrapunovo, boarding at Orekhovo-Zuevo and getting off at Khrapunovo.

reading.question: What is Pyotr's answer every time Venichka asks whether there is anything left to drink?
options: That there is one bottle left
That the buffet car is still open
That he is hiding some for later
reading.explain: Both times Venichka asks, Pyotr repeats that there is nothing — it has all been drunk.

reading.ru: Кружится у меня почему-то в голове Антон Чехов.
reading.question: Which writers keep spinning round in Venichka's head as he tries to collect his main thought?
reading.explain: He names Chekhov first, then Schiller, and admits he has no idea why.

reading.ru: Да, вот он при чем: когда ему водку случалось пить, он ноги свои опускал в шампанское.
reading.question: What does Venichka say Schiller used to do when he drank vodka?
options: Put on slippers and a dressing gown
Sit down to write a tragedy
reading.explain: Venichka first attaches the detail to writing tragedies, then corrects himself: Schiller put his feet in champagne when he drank vodka.

reading.ru: А Чехов Антон перед смертью сказал: «Выпить хочу».
reading.question: What does Venichka claim Chekhov said just before he died?
reading.explain: Venichka reports Chekhov's dying words as «Выпить хочу» — and then he died.

reading.ru: То есть, если перевести это на хороший язык: «Кто же сейчас не пьет?»
reading.question: How does Venichka translate Hegel's sentence about differences into 'good language'?
options: "There is being, but by what name to call it?"
reading.explain: After quoting Hegel on degrees of difference, he renders the whole thing as a question about who abstains these days.

reading.question: How long does Venichka say he dozed, unsure whether he was falling asleep or waking up?
options: He does not say at all
reading.explain: He gives the oddly precise but useless estimate of 12 or 35 minutes.

reading.ru: А когда очнулся – в вагоне не было ни души, и Петр куда-то исчез.
reading.question: What does Venichka find when he comes to after dozing?
options: The carriage is empty and Pyotr has vanished
Pyotr is sitting beside him with a bottle
The train has stopped at Khrapunovo
reading.correct: The carriage is empty and Pyotr has vanished
reading.explain: There is not a soul in the carriage, yet he can hear doors banging throughout the train.

reading.ru: Но он уже выпрыгнул в окошко.
reading.question: How does Pyotr leave the carriage after putting out the lights?
options: He jumps out of the window
He walks out through the door
He gets off at the next station
reading.correct: He jumps out of the window
reading.explain: He goes down the carriage extinguishing the lights and then jumps out of the window, answering Venichka from outside.

reading.ru: Вместе со мною вздрогнули и забились вагоны.
reading.question: What happens at the same moment as Venichka clutches his temples and starts shaking?
options: The carriages shudder and shake too
The lights all come back on
The train comes to a stop
reading.correct: The carriages shudder and shake too
reading.explain: The chapter ends with the carriages shaking along with him — and the remark that they had in fact been shaking for a long time already.

highlight.question: Which sentence says where the princess got ON the train?
sentences: В Храпунове вышла.
Она из Петушков ехала в Храпуново.
В Орехово-Зуеве вошла, а в Храпунове – вышла.
highlight.explain: Only the last sentence names Orekhovo-Zuevo as the station where she boarded.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives Venichka's plain-language translation of Hegel's saying?
sentences: Отведи глаза, пошляк, не смотри.
Я мысли собираю, а ты – смотришь.
Вот еще Гегель был.
Это я очень хорошо помню: был Гегель.
Он говорил: «Нет различий, кроме различия в степени между различными степенями и отсутствием различия».
То есть, если перевести это на хороший язык: «Кто же сейчас не пьет?»
Есть у нас что-нибудь выпить, Петр?
highlight.explain: The sixth sentence recasts Hegel's formula as the question about who doesn't drink nowadays.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why the banging of doors seemed strange to Venichka?
sentences: А когда очнулся – в вагоне не было ни души, и Петр куда-то исчез.
Поезд все мчался сквозь дождь и черноту.
Странно было слышать хлопанье дверей во всех вагонах: оттого странно, что ведь ни в одном вагоне нет ни души…
highlight.explain: The third sentence states the reason: there is not a soul in any carriage, so nobody could be banging the doors.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells Venichka to go and sell his sunflower seeds?
sentences: Ничего!
Оставайся!
Оставайся тут, бабуленька!
Оставайся, старая стерва!
Поезжай в Москву!
Продавай свои семечки!
А я не могу больше, не могу-у-у-у…
highlight.explain: In his final outburst Pyotr orders him to sell his seeds before saying he cannot go on.
